The original source is preserved; no experiment, endpoint bound, or record bound changed. INTERVENTION CLOSURE BEFORE A COARSE LIMIT Private ASTRA-FRESH-20261023 / P1. 23 October 2026 UTC. Root extension of uniform_design's Brownian/Fourier counterexample. All previous spin, response, measurement, memory, and Green sources remain unchanged. This is a separate exact Gaussian construction, not a claim that the counterexample belongs to the regional copying-spin class. MAIN RESULT There is a family of classical stochastic systems indexed by one constitutive parameter eta in [-1,1] with the following properties: (i) They start in exactly the same full state. Their Markov semigroups are uniformly close, at every state, on every fixed degree of a common contractive observable algebra. (ii) Their complete noisy records become indistinguishable under EVERY precommitted experiment in a specified bounded-energy probe class, uniformly over arbitrarily moving probes in that class. (iii) One causal bounded-energy experiment has a limiting output law that retains eta at order one. In particular eta=1 and eta=0 have a strictly positive limiting total-variation separation. Thus identifying models by the precommitted coarse limit and then allowing adaptive choice of experiments can lose a physically observable parameter. The order of these operations matters. A fixed measurement-energy budget alone does not justify this adaptive closure. The example explicitly charges an exponentially large available probe bank and a d-bit selector; it does not prove an inexpensive physical implementation or a limitation under additional locality, bandwidth, or restricted-action hypotheses. 1. A SHARED FULL STATE SPACE AND WELL-DEFINED DYNAMICS Fix d>=1 and let S_d={-1,+1}^d. There are d base angle coordinates U_i and 2^d bank angle coordinates V_s, all in the circle R/(2pi Z). The full state space is the product torus of dimension d+2^d. Set every angle initially to zero. Two independent d-dimensional standard Brownian motions W and W' generate, during a unit preparatory activity interval, U_i(t)=W_i(t) modulo 2pi, V_s^eta(t)=d^(-1/2) sum_i s_i [eta W_i(t)+sqrt(1-eta^2)W'_i(t)] modulo 2pi. (1.1) At time one, freeze all hidden dynamics. The later experiment has no hidden backaction: it only observes bounded functions of these frozen coordinates. One may equivalently describe the family on the FULL torus by constant diffusion vector fields, starting from any initial torus point. Real lifts in (1.1) are proof variables; the controller never observes an unwrapped angle. No rationality condition on sqrt(d) is required for constant vector fields on a torus. Let S be the 2^d by d matrix with entries S_(s,i)=s_i/sqrt(d). The covariance matrix of the torus diffusion is C_eta = [ I_d eta S^T eta S S S^T ]. (1.2) It is positive semidefinite for |eta|<=1 by the explicit construction (1.1). Its diagonal entries are one. The entire marginal law of the base block is independent of eta; the entire marginal law of the bank block is also independent of eta. Only their cross-dependence changes. For clarity the common control family needed below permits deterministic activity 0<=a(t)<=1 with total active time at most one. Its generator is a(t) times the constant-covariance heat generator. The actual separating experiment takes a=1 on [0,1] and zero thereafter. No arbitrary unlisted physical intervention is included in the precommitted comparison. 2. UNIFORM ALGEBRA AND ENDPOINT CERTIFICATE Let A_D be the real trigonometric polynomials with Fourier frequencies z=(u,v) in Z^d x Z^(2^d) of total l1 degree |u|_1+|v|_1<=D. Use conjugate coefficient symmetry to make functions real, and norm ||f||_alg=sum_z |f_hat(z)|. This norm dominates sup norm, has ||1||=1, and is submultiplicative; multiplication adds total degree. The Fourier mode exp(i z dot theta) has generator eigenvalue -q_eta(z), where q_eta(z)=z^T C_eta z/2>=0. Each heat semigroup therefore preserves degree and contracts this norm. For two parameters eta,xi, |q_eta(u,v)-q_xi(u,v)| =|eta-xi| |u dot S^T v| <= |eta-xi| |u|_1 |v|_1/sqrt(d) <= |eta-xi| D^2/(4sqrt(d)). (2.1) The map q->exp(-tau q) is tau-Lipschitz for q>=0. Hence, from EVERY common initial full torus state and on any interval of active length tau, ||P_eta(t,t+h)f-P_xi(t,t+h)f||_infinity <= ||f||_alg |eta-xi| tau D^2/(4sqrt(d)). (2.2) The comparison projection is the identity. Exact initial joint agreement is consequently literal, not only agreement of observed means or marginals. The bound holds on the full state space, even away from the particular Gaussian submanifolds reached from zero. Each coordinate sine belongs to A_1 with norm one and is bounded by one. During preparation its drift has magnitude at most 1/2 and its quadratic variation density is at most one; after freezing both are zero. The hidden paths are continuous. These are the required scalar modulus bounds. Signed l1-bounded linear combinations of coordinate sines retain the same bounds: the covariance matrix is PSD with unit diagonal, so every entry has absolute value at most one. The construction therefore satisfies the earlier abstract algebra/endpoint/modulus conditions for each fixed probe or finite bank. 3. ALL PRECOMMITTED EXPERIMENTS IN THE DECLARED CLASS AGREE IN THE LIMIT At each t let phi_t be a deterministic real member of A_1 with ||phi_t||_alg<=1; in particular |phi_t|<=1. Allow arbitrary measurable time-dependence, without a visit-count or variation bound. Let deterministic H satisfy int_0^T H_t^2 dt<=Gamma, and observe dY_t=H_t phi_t(theta_t)dt+dB_t, (3.1) with independent observation Brownian noise. Fix the horizon T and total activity at most one. This includes all precommitted moving sine probes used by the separating experiment before its final record-dependent choice. The target algebra is contractive under propagation and multiplication. For r observation times, the temporal telescope uses (2.2) on disjoint time gaps; their total ACTIVE length is at most one. The whole continuation has degree at most r and norm at most one. Thus |E_eta product_(j=1)^r phi_(t_j)(theta_(t_j)) -E_xi product_(j=1)^r phi_(t_j)(theta_(t_j))| <= |eta-xi| r^2/(4sqrt(d)). (3.2) This is uniform in all times and choices of probes. Keeping the active-time sum avoids an unnecessary extra factor r. Repeated times only reduce the number of transition gaps. Initial full-state agreement removes the initial law term. The elementary Gaussian overlap identity for deterministic independent hidden signals gives, for their record densities ell_eta,ell_xi relative to Wiener measure, ||ell_eta-ell_xi||_2^2 =sum_(r>=1)1/r! int_[0,T]^r [E_eta product_j H_(t_j)phi_(t_j)(theta_(t_j)) -E_xi product_j H_(t_j)phi_(t_j)(theta_(t_j))]^2 dt. It follows that sup_precommitted TV(P_eta^Y,P_xi^Y) <= |eta-xi|/(8sqrt(d)) sqrt{exp(Gamma)[Gamma+7Gamma^2+6Gamma^3+Gamma^4]}. (3.3) The bound may always be capped by one. At Gamma=0 it is zero. The polynomial in brackets is the fourth Touchard polynomial, from sum r^4 Gamma^r/r!=exp(Gamma)(Gamma+7Gamma^2+6Gamma^3+Gamma^4). Independent public randomization over complete schedules is also allowed by conditioning on the coins. It does not license record-dependent schedules. Consequently ALL eta in [-1,1] are identified by this precommitted bounded-energy observational limit. This is an operational uniform record statement, stronger than agreement on individual fixed-degree moments. 4. ONE CAUSAL EXPERIMENT THAT RETAINS ETA Use the horizon [0,3]. Prepare the hidden field on [0,1] as above with H=0. Write U_i=W_i(1), independent N(0,1) real lifts. On the d successive intervals of length 1/d partitioning [1,2], observe sin(U_i) at gain sqrt(Gamma_1). The normalized interval increments are exactly R_i=Z_i+sqrt(Gamma_1/d) sin(U_i), (4.1) where the Z_i are independent standard normals, independent of the hidden preparation. Set s_i=sign(R_i), with any convention at zero. At time two the controller knows s from the record. On [2,3] it reads the single bank probe sin(V_s^eta) at gain sqrt(Gamma_2). Its final unit-interval increment is Y_final=sqrt(Gamma_2)sin(A_d^eta)+Z_0, (4.2) where A_d^eta is the real lift selected from (1.1), and Z_0 is a fresh independent standard normal. The full signal energy is Gamma_1+Gamma_2, independent of d. The policy is causal, uses no hidden state, and is exactly the SAME algorithm for every eta. The preparation history, the scan schedule and its gains are common. The only record-dependent operation is the final address of a bounded local bank readout. Its address has d bits and the available bank has 2^d entries. No bounded hardware, addressing cost, or measurement bandwidth is claimed. 5. EXACT SELECTED-ANGLE LIMIT AND OPERATIONAL PREDICTION Put epsilon_d=sqrt(Gamma_1/d) and A_d^1=d^(-1/2)sum_i U_i sign(Z_i+epsilon_d sin U_i). For a standard normal U and real t define a_d(t)=exp[-t^2/(2d)], b_d(t)=E{sin(tU/sqrt(d))[2Phi(epsilon_d sin U)-1]}. Independence of the d pairs (U_i,Z_i) gives the exact identity E exp(i t A_d^1)=[a_d(t)+i b_d(t)]^d. (5.1) Let c=sqrt(2/pi). The identity 2Phi(z)-1=c int_0^z exp(-v^2/2)dv implies |2Phi(z)-1-cz|<=c|z|^3/6. Therefore |b_d(t)-c sqrt(Gamma_1/d) exp[-(1+t^2/d)/2]sinh(t/sqrt(d))| <=Gamma_1^(3/2)|t|/(3pi d^2). (5.2) Here E sin(alpha U)sin U=exp[-(1+alpha^2)/2]sinh(alpha), and |sin(tU/sqrt(d))|<=|tU|/sqrt(d). These give every constant in (5.2). Set m=sqrt(2Gamma_1/pi)exp(-1/2). For fixed t, a_d(t)=1-t^2/(2d)+O_t(d^-2) and b_d(t)=tm/d+O_(t,Gamma_1)(d^-2). Thus (5.1) converges to exp(-t^2/2+i tm), proving A_d^1 ==> N(m,1). (5.3) Conditional on the ENTIRE base-plus-scan sigma-field, the variable Z'_d=d^(-1/2)sum_i s_i W'_i(1) has exactly the N(0,1) law, independent of that sigma-field. This follows because its conditional variance is d^(-1)sum_i s_i^2=1 and W' is independent. Hence exactly A_d^eta=eta A_d^1+sqrt(1-eta^2) Z'_d, A_d^eta ==> N(eta m,1). (5.4) The limiting final-record prediction is consequently Y_final ==> sqrt(Gamma_2) sin(G_eta)+Z_0, G_eta~N(eta m,1), Z_0~N(0,1) independent. (5.5) In particular its mean tends to sqrt(Gamma_2) exp(-1/2) sin(eta m). (5.6) Boundedness of sin and the Gaussian observation noise justify passing to this mean. Choosing Gamma_1=pi e/8 gives m=1/2, for which (5.6) is strictly increasing in eta on [-1,1]. The previously erased constitutive parameter therefore affects an actual specified experimental prediction. 6. A BOUNDED-TEST TOTAL-VARIATION SEPARATION Take Gamma_1=pi e/8 and Gamma_2=1. Write mu=exp(-1/2)sin(1/2)>1/6. For eta=0 the selected angle is exactly N(0,1), independent of the scan, so E_0 sin(Y_final)=0 for every d by symmetry. For eta=1, integration over Z_0 gives E_1 sin(Y_final)=exp(-1/2) E sin(sin(A_d^1)). Since |sin z-z|<=|z|^3/6 and |sin(A_d^1)|<=1, liminf_(d->infinity) E_1 sin(Y_final) >=exp(-1/2)(mu-1/6)>0. The test sin(Y_final) is bounded in [-1,1]. It is a measurable function of the COMPLETE record, so liminf_(d->infinity) TV(P_1^adaptive,P_0^adaptive) >= [exp(-1/2)/2][exp(-1/2)sin(1/2)-1/6] = approximately 0.03764117797. (6.1) The decimal only evaluates the exact analytic lower bound; it is not a simulation or acquired measurement. A scaled sine test can improve the constant, but positivity already resolves the scientific implication. Combining (3.3) and (6.1) proves a genuine separation between the declared precommitted and adaptive experiment classes at fixed time and energy. It is not merely a failed proof norm or a failed Gaussian-overlap identity. 7. WHAT ADDITIONAL REPRESENTATION THIS EXAMPLE REQUIRES The actual commands and observed controls are the same under all eta. More accurate storage of that command history cannot infer a coupling parameter which the coarse model has discarded. The retained base marginal and bank marginal laws likewise do not recover it. Their cross-dependence is the missing physical interface. Within this explicitly parametrized Gaussian family, retaining eta preserves the limiting prediction (5.5) for this protocol. This is a one-parameter constitutive repair. It is not a theorem that eta alone, or any fixed number of posterior coordinates, suffices for every conceivable future adaptive protocol. It also does not convert the exponentially rich bank into a cheap device or a local spatial model. The lesson for an effective theory is precise: the observable quotient used to identify microscopic models must survive the admitted adaptive selection of future experiments. Uniformity over every PRECOMMITTED schedule is still insufficient when the intervention class can choose from this growing bank. The sequence and scope of the allowed experiments are part of the claim that a physical description is predictive. 8. RELATION TO THE POSITIVE REGIONAL CONSTRUCTION The previously proved regional copying-spin field retains slow regional means and causal public pair responses. Its coefficient-l1 polynomial certificate gives complete-record prediction for a fixed finite bank under arbitrary admitted feedback, and for arbitrary moving probes under precommitted schedules. The countable-profile selection theorem also permits genuine feedback among a charged family of complete schedules. The present counterexample satisfies the ABSTRACT algebra/endpoint/scalar- modulus hypotheses, so those hypotheses alone cannot extend that theorem to an unrestricted adaptive moving bank. However its covariance is strongly nonlocal: base and bank have coordinated common noise. The copying-spin field has diagonal instantaneous regional brackets and positive bounded-row migration. This proof does NOT defeat that additional structure. The consequential missing question is now narrower: can the physical positive-migration/diagonal-noise structure control the selection-sensitive cross-dependence that the abstract norm overlooks? A proof would need an adapted stochastic or two-replica comparison using that extra structure. An arbitrary-algebra extension is ruled out by (6.1); a return to merely improving its universal constants cannot repair it. 9. PREDECESSORS AND NOVELTY SCOPE Polynomial semigroup closure and moment representations in state dimensions controlled by moment degree are established mathematical tools; see Cuchiero, Keller-Ressel and Teichmann, arXiv:0812.4740v2, and Cuchiero, Larsson and Svaluto-Ferro, arXiv:1807.03229v1. The Gaussian replica likelihood identity and its moment expansion also have standard predecessors; a direct finite-dimensional presentation is Kunisky, Wein and Bandeira, arXiv:1907.11636v1, Proposition 2.5 and Theorem 2.6. The fact that adaptive selection can change statistical validity has a large existing literature. Russo and Zou, AISTATS 2016, Proposition 1 and Section 4, give information-based bounds on adaptive selection bias. The present source does not claim that broad insight as new. It instead proves the displayed continuous-time all-state algebra/record comparison and an explicit failure of its unrestricted adaptive closure, with exact common initial state and fixed observation energy. No literature-wide priority assertion is made. Original mathematical scope, independent proof checking, empirical validation, and novelty are separate. No empirical measurement or practical advantage has been established here; priority of this precise construction is UNKNOWN. END OF SOURCE

Intervention Closure Before A Coarse Limit V2
CLARIFIED V2: the admitted activity is explicitly bounded by one, as
required for the common instantaneous scalar modulus. The original source
is preserved; no experiment, endpoint bound, or record bound changed.

INTERVENTION CLOSURE BEFORE A COARSE LIMIT

Private ASTRA-FRESH-20261023 / P1. 23 October 2026 UTC.
Root extension of uniform_design's Brownian/Fourier counterexample.
All previous spin, response, measurement, memory, and Green sources remain
unchanged. This is a separate exact Gaussian construction, not a claim that
the counterexample belongs to the regional copying-spin class.

MAIN RESULT

There is a family of classical stochastic systems indexed by one constitutive
parameter eta in [-1,1] with the following properties:

  (i) They start in exactly the same full state. Their Markov semigroups are
      uniformly close, at every state, on every fixed degree of a common
      contractive observable algebra.

 (ii) Their complete noisy records become indistinguishable under EVERY
      precommitted experiment in a specified bounded-energy probe class,
      uniformly over arbitrarily moving probes in that class.

(iii) One causal bounded-energy experiment has a limiting output law that
      retains eta at order one. In particular eta=1 and eta=0 have a strictly
      positive limiting total-variation separation.

Thus identifying models by the precommitted coarse limit and then allowing
adaptive choice of experiments can lose a physically observable parameter.
The order of these operations matters. A fixed measurement-energy budget
alone does not justify this adaptive closure. The example explicitly charges
an exponentially large available probe bank and a d-bit selector; it does
not prove an inexpensive physical implementation or a limitation under
additional locality, bandwidth, or restricted-action hypotheses.

1. A SHARED FULL STATE SPACE AND WELL-DEFINED DYNAMICS

Fix d>=1 and let S_d={-1,+1}^d. There are d base angle coordinates U_i and
2^d bank angle coordinates V_s, all in the circle R/(2pi Z). The full state
space is the product torus of dimension d+2^d. Set every angle initially to
zero. Two independent d-dimensional standard Brownian motions W and W'
generate, during a unit preparatory activity interval,

 U_i(t)=W_i(t) modulo 2pi,
 V_s^eta(t)=d^(-1/2) sum_i s_i
                   [eta W_i(t)+sqrt(1-eta^2)W'_i(t)] modulo 2pi.       (1.1)

At time one, freeze all hidden dynamics. The later experiment has no hidden
backaction: it only observes bounded functions of these frozen coordinates.
One may equivalently describe the family on the FULL torus by constant
diffusion vector fields, starting from any initial torus point. Real lifts
in (1.1) are proof variables; the controller never observes an unwrapped angle.
No rationality condition on sqrt(d) is required for constant vector fields
on a torus.

Let S be the 2^d by d matrix with entries S_(s,i)=s_i/sqrt(d). The covariance
matrix of the torus diffusion is

                 C_eta = [ I_d       eta S^T
                           eta S      S S^T ].                       (1.2)

It is positive semidefinite for |eta|<=1 by the explicit construction (1.1).
Its diagonal entries are one. The entire marginal law of the base block is
independent of eta; the entire marginal law of the bank block is also
independent of eta. Only their cross-dependence changes.

For clarity the common control family needed below permits deterministic
activity 0<=a(t)<=1 with total active time at most one. Its generator is
a(t) times the constant-covariance heat generator. The actual separating
experiment takes a=1 on [0,1] and zero thereafter. No arbitrary unlisted
physical intervention is included in the precommitted comparison.

2. UNIFORM ALGEBRA AND ENDPOINT CERTIFICATE

Let A_D be the real trigonometric polynomials with Fourier frequencies
z=(u,v) in Z^d x Z^(2^d) of total l1 degree |u|_1+|v|_1<=D. Use conjugate
coefficient symmetry to make functions real, and norm

           ||f||_alg=sum_z |f_hat(z)|.

This norm dominates sup norm, has ||1||=1, and is submultiplicative;
multiplication adds total degree. The Fourier mode exp(i z dot theta) has
generator eigenvalue -q_eta(z), where q_eta(z)=z^T C_eta z/2>=0. Each heat
semigroup therefore preserves degree and contracts this norm.

For two parameters eta,xi,

 |q_eta(u,v)-q_xi(u,v)|
   =|eta-xi| |u dot S^T v|
   <= |eta-xi| |u|_1 |v|_1/sqrt(d)
   <= |eta-xi| D^2/(4sqrt(d)).                                      (2.1)

The map q->exp(-tau q) is tau-Lipschitz for q>=0. Hence, from EVERY common
initial full torus state and on any interval of active length tau,

 ||P_eta(t,t+h)f-P_xi(t,t+h)f||_infinity
       <= ||f||_alg |eta-xi| tau D^2/(4sqrt(d)).                     (2.2)

The comparison projection is the identity. Exact initial joint agreement
is consequently literal, not only agreement of observed means or marginals.
The bound holds on the full state space, even away from the particular
Gaussian submanifolds reached from zero.

Each coordinate sine belongs to A_1 with norm one and is bounded by one.
During preparation its drift has magnitude at most 1/2 and its quadratic
variation density is at most one; after freezing both are zero. The hidden
paths are continuous. These are the required scalar modulus bounds. Signed
l1-bounded linear combinations of coordinate sines retain the same bounds:
the covariance matrix is PSD with unit diagonal, so every entry has absolute
value at most one. The construction therefore satisfies the earlier abstract
algebra/endpoint/modulus conditions for each fixed probe or finite bank.

3. ALL PRECOMMITTED EXPERIMENTS IN THE DECLARED CLASS AGREE IN THE LIMIT

At each t let phi_t be a deterministic real member of A_1 with
||phi_t||_alg<=1; in particular |phi_t|<=1. Allow arbitrary measurable
time-dependence, without a visit-count or variation bound. Let deterministic
H satisfy int_0^T H_t^2 dt<=Gamma, and observe

                 dY_t=H_t phi_t(theta_t)dt+dB_t,                    (3.1)

with independent observation Brownian noise. Fix the horizon T and total
activity at most one. This includes all precommitted moving sine probes
used by the separating experiment before its final record-dependent choice.

The target algebra is contractive under propagation and multiplication.
For r observation times, the temporal telescope uses (2.2) on disjoint
time gaps; their total ACTIVE length is at most one. The whole continuation
has degree at most r and norm at most one. Thus

 |E_eta product_(j=1)^r phi_(t_j)(theta_(t_j))
       -E_xi product_(j=1)^r phi_(t_j)(theta_(t_j))|
                     <= |eta-xi| r^2/(4sqrt(d)).                   (3.2)

This is uniform in all times and choices of probes. Keeping the active-time
sum avoids an unnecessary extra factor r. Repeated times only reduce the
number of transition gaps. Initial full-state agreement removes the initial
law term.

The elementary Gaussian overlap identity for deterministic independent hidden
signals gives, for their record densities ell_eta,ell_xi relative to Wiener
measure,

 ||ell_eta-ell_xi||_2^2
  =sum_(r>=1)1/r! int_[0,T]^r
     [E_eta product_j H_(t_j)phi_(t_j)(theta_(t_j))
      -E_xi product_j H_(t_j)phi_(t_j)(theta_(t_j))]^2 dt.

It follows that

 sup_precommitted TV(P_eta^Y,P_xi^Y)
  <= |eta-xi|/(8sqrt(d))
           sqrt{exp(Gamma)[Gamma+7Gamma^2+6Gamma^3+Gamma^4]}.        (3.3)

The bound may always be capped by one. At Gamma=0 it is zero. The polynomial
in brackets is the fourth Touchard polynomial, from
sum r^4 Gamma^r/r!=exp(Gamma)(Gamma+7Gamma^2+6Gamma^3+Gamma^4).
Independent public randomization over complete schedules is also allowed by
conditioning on the coins. It does not license record-dependent schedules.

Consequently ALL eta in [-1,1] are identified by this precommitted
bounded-energy observational limit. This is an operational uniform record
statement, stronger than agreement on individual fixed-degree moments.

4. ONE CAUSAL EXPERIMENT THAT RETAINS ETA

Use the horizon [0,3]. Prepare the hidden field on [0,1] as above with H=0.
Write U_i=W_i(1), independent N(0,1) real lifts. On the d successive intervals
of length 1/d partitioning [1,2], observe sin(U_i) at gain sqrt(Gamma_1).
The normalized interval increments are exactly

              R_i=Z_i+sqrt(Gamma_1/d) sin(U_i),                    (4.1)

where the Z_i are independent standard normals, independent of the hidden
preparation. Set s_i=sign(R_i), with any convention at zero. At time two the
controller knows s from the record. On [2,3] it reads the single bank probe
sin(V_s^eta) at gain sqrt(Gamma_2). Its final unit-interval increment is

              Y_final=sqrt(Gamma_2)sin(A_d^eta)+Z_0,               (4.2)

where A_d^eta is the real lift selected from (1.1), and Z_0 is a fresh
independent standard normal. The full signal energy is Gamma_1+Gamma_2,
independent of d. The policy is causal, uses no hidden state, and is exactly
the SAME algorithm for every eta.

The preparation history, the scan schedule and its gains are common. The
only record-dependent operation is the final address of a bounded local
bank readout. Its address has d bits and the available bank has 2^d entries.
No bounded hardware, addressing cost, or measurement bandwidth is claimed.

5. EXACT SELECTED-ANGLE LIMIT AND OPERATIONAL PREDICTION

Put epsilon_d=sqrt(Gamma_1/d) and

           A_d^1=d^(-1/2)sum_i U_i sign(Z_i+epsilon_d sin U_i).

For a standard normal U and real t define

 a_d(t)=exp[-t^2/(2d)],
 b_d(t)=E{sin(tU/sqrt(d))[2Phi(epsilon_d sin U)-1]}.

Independence of the d pairs (U_i,Z_i) gives the exact identity

                    E exp(i t A_d^1)=[a_d(t)+i b_d(t)]^d.          (5.1)

Let c=sqrt(2/pi). The identity
2Phi(z)-1=c int_0^z exp(-v^2/2)dv implies
|2Phi(z)-1-cz|<=c|z|^3/6. Therefore

 |b_d(t)-c sqrt(Gamma_1/d)
       exp[-(1+t^2/d)/2]sinh(t/sqrt(d))|
                <=Gamma_1^(3/2)|t|/(3pi d^2).                    (5.2)

Here E sin(alpha U)sin U=exp[-(1+alpha^2)/2]sinh(alpha), and
|sin(tU/sqrt(d))|<=|tU|/sqrt(d). These give every constant in (5.2).

Set m=sqrt(2Gamma_1/pi)exp(-1/2). For fixed t,
a_d(t)=1-t^2/(2d)+O_t(d^-2) and b_d(t)=tm/d+O_(t,Gamma_1)(d^-2).
Thus (5.1) converges to exp(-t^2/2+i tm), proving

                          A_d^1 ==> N(m,1).                       (5.3)

Conditional on the ENTIRE base-plus-scan sigma-field, the variable
Z'_d=d^(-1/2)sum_i s_i W'_i(1) has exactly the N(0,1) law, independent of
that sigma-field. This follows because its conditional variance is
d^(-1)sum_i s_i^2=1 and W' is independent. Hence exactly

           A_d^eta=eta A_d^1+sqrt(1-eta^2) Z'_d,
                         A_d^eta ==> N(eta m,1).                   (5.4)

The limiting final-record prediction is consequently

       Y_final ==> sqrt(Gamma_2) sin(G_eta)+Z_0,
                   G_eta~N(eta m,1), Z_0~N(0,1) independent.       (5.5)

In particular its mean tends to

              sqrt(Gamma_2) exp(-1/2) sin(eta m).                 (5.6)

Boundedness of sin and the Gaussian observation noise justify passing to
this mean. Choosing Gamma_1=pi e/8 gives m=1/2, for which (5.6) is strictly
increasing in eta on [-1,1]. The previously erased constitutive parameter
therefore affects an actual specified experimental prediction.

6. A BOUNDED-TEST TOTAL-VARIATION SEPARATION

Take Gamma_1=pi e/8 and Gamma_2=1. Write

              mu=exp(-1/2)sin(1/2)>1/6.

For eta=0 the selected angle is exactly N(0,1), independent of the scan,
so E_0 sin(Y_final)=0 for every d by symmetry. For eta=1, integration over
Z_0 gives

       E_1 sin(Y_final)=exp(-1/2) E sin(sin(A_d^1)).

Since |sin z-z|<=|z|^3/6 and |sin(A_d^1)|<=1,

 liminf_(d->infinity) E_1 sin(Y_final)
                          >=exp(-1/2)(mu-1/6)>0.

The test sin(Y_final) is bounded in [-1,1]. It is a measurable function of
the COMPLETE record, so

 liminf_(d->infinity) TV(P_1^adaptive,P_0^adaptive)
             >= [exp(-1/2)/2][exp(-1/2)sin(1/2)-1/6]

INTERVENTION CLOSURE BEFORE A COARSE LIMIT

Private ASTRA-FRESH-20261023 / P1. 23 October 2026 UTC.
Root extension of uniform_design's Brownian/Fourier counterexample.
All previous spin, response, measurement, memory, and Green sources remain
unchanged. This is a separate exact Gaussian construction, not a claim that
the counterexample belongs to the regional copying-spin class.

MAIN RESULT

There is a family of classical stochastic systems indexed by one constitutive
parameter eta in [-1,1] with the following properties:

  (i) They start in exactly the same full state. Their Markov semigroups are
      uniformly close, at every state, on every fixed degree of a common
      contractive observable algebra.

 (ii) Their complete noisy records become indistinguishable under EVERY
      precommitted experiment in a specified bounded-energy probe class,
      uniformly over arbitrarily moving probes in that class.

(iii) One causal bounded-energy experiment has a limiting output law that
      retains eta at order one. In particular eta=1 and eta=0 have a strictly
      positive limiting total-variation separation.

Thus identifying models by the precommitted coarse limit and then allowing
adaptive choice of experiments can lose a physically observable parameter.
The order of these operations matters. A fixed measurement-energy budget
alone does not justify this adaptive closure. The example explicitly charges
an exponentially large available probe bank and a d-bit selector; it does
not prove an inexpensive physical implementation or a limitation under
additional locality, bandwidth, or restricted-action hypotheses.

1. A SHARED FULL STATE SPACE AND WELL-DEFINED DYNAMICS

Fix d>=1 and let S_d={-1,+1}^d. There are d base angle coordinates U_i and
2^d bank angle coordinates V_s, all in the circle R/(2pi Z). The full state
space is the product torus of dimension d+2^d. Set every angle initially to
zero. Two independent d-dimensional standard Brownian motions W and W'
generate, during a unit preparatory activity interval,

 U_i(t)=W_i(t) modulo 2pi,
 V_s^eta(t)=d^(-1/2) sum_i s_i
                   [eta W_i(t)+sqrt(1-eta^2)W'_i(t)] modulo 2pi.       (1.1)

At time one, freeze all hidden dynamics. The later experiment has no hidden
backaction: it only observes bounded functions of these frozen coordinates.
One may equivalently describe the family on the FULL torus by constant
diffusion vector fields, starting from any initial torus point. Real lifts
in (1.1) are proof variables; the controller never observes an unwrapped angle.
No rationality condition on sqrt(d) is required for constant vector fields
on a torus.

Let S be the 2^d by d matrix with entries S_(s,i)=s_i/sqrt(d). The covariance
matrix of the torus diffusion is

                 C_eta = [ I_d       eta S^T
                           eta S      S S^T ].                       (1.2)

It is positive semidefinite for |eta|<=1 by the explicit construction (1.1).
Its diagonal entries are one. The entire marginal law of the base block is
independent of eta; the entire marginal law of the bank block is also
independent of eta. Only their cross-dependence changes.

For clarity the common control family needed below permits deterministic
activity 0<=a(t)<=1 with total active time at most one. Its generator is
a(t) times the constant-covariance heat generator. The actual separating
experiment takes a=1 on [0,1] and zero thereafter. No arbitrary unlisted
physical intervention is included in the precommitted comparison.

2. UNIFORM ALGEBRA AND ENDPOINT CERTIFICATE

Let A_D be the real trigonometric polynomials with Fourier frequencies
z=(u,v) in Z^d x Z^(2^d) of total l1 degree |u|_1+|v|_1<=D. Use conjugate
coefficient symmetry to make functions real, and norm

           ||f||_alg=sum_z |f_hat(z)|.

This norm dominates sup norm, has ||1||=1, and is submultiplicative;
multiplication adds total degree. The Fourier mode exp(i z dot theta) has
generator eigenvalue -q_eta(z), where q_eta(z)=z^T C_eta z/2>=0. Each heat
semigroup therefore preserves degree and contracts this norm.

For two parameters eta,xi,

 |q_eta(u,v)-q_xi(u,v)|
   =|eta-xi| |u dot S^T v|
   <= |eta-xi| |u|_1 |v|_1/sqrt(d)
   <= |eta-xi| D^2/(4sqrt(d)).                                      (2.1)

The map q->exp(-tau q) is tau-Lipschitz for q>=0. Hence, from EVERY common
initial full torus state and on any interval of active length tau,

 ||P_eta(t,t+h)f-P_xi(t,t+h)f||_infinity
       <= ||f||_alg |eta-xi| tau D^2/(4sqrt(d)).                     (2.2)

The comparison projection is the identity. Exact initial joint agreement
is consequently literal, not only agreement of observed means or marginals.
The bound holds on the full state space, even away from the particular
Gaussian submanifolds reached from zero.

Each coordinate sine belongs to A_1 with norm one and is bounded by one.
During preparation its drift has magnitude at most 1/2 and its quadratic
variation density is at most one; after freezing both are zero. The hidden
paths are continuous. These are the required scalar modulus bounds. Signed
l1-bounded linear combinations of coordinate sines retain the same bounds:
the covariance matrix is PSD with unit diagonal, so every entry has absolute
value at most one. The construction therefore satisfies the earlier abstract
algebra/endpoint/modulus conditions for each fixed probe or finite bank.

3. ALL PRECOMMITTED EXPERIMENTS IN THE DECLARED CLASS AGREE IN THE LIMIT

||phi_t||_alg<=1; in particular |phi_t|<=1. Allow arbitrary measurable
time-dependence, without a visit-count or variation bound. Let deterministic

                 dY_t=H_t phi_t(theta_t)dt+dB_t,                    (3.1)

activity at most one. This includes all precommitted moving sine probes

conditioning on the coins. It does not license record-dependent schedules.

bounded-energy observational limit. This is an operational uniform record
statement, stronger than agreement on individual fixed-degree moments.

The preparation history, the scan schedule and its gains are common. The
only record-dependent operation is the final address of a bounded local
bank readout. Its address has d bits and the available bank has 2^d entries.
No bounded hardware, addressing cost, or measurement bandwidth is claimed.

           A_d^1=d^(-1/2)sum_i U_i sign(Z_i+epsilon_d sin U_i).

In particular its mean tends to

increasing in eta on [-1,1]. The previously erased constitutive parameter
